newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Chinese urged not to infiltrate Australian party.
newsitem.headline: Chinese urged not to infiltrate Australian party.

text.p: A leading Chinese Australian spoke out on Monday against a plan to have thousands of Chinese join a party being formed by anti-immigration politician Pauline Hanson and then vote to dump her from it.

In an editorial due to be published this week, details of which have already been reported, the Chinese Weekly newspaper will tell its readers that they owe it to Australia to sign up with Hanson's fledgling One Nation party.
But Henry Tsang, deputy lord mayor of Sydney, said in a statement on Monday that the plan was too risky.
"The idea sounds good in principle. However, reality dictates that it should not proceed," Tsang said.
"Firstly, I have significant concerns with Chinese community members sending their names, addresses and telephone numbers to a right-wing fundamentalist party with racist overtones.
"Such a situation could prove to be very dangerous. Who knows who has access to the One Nation mailing list?

"More importantly, if Chinese community members sign up with One Nation, Pauline Hanson can turn around and claim she has Chinese community support for her party. This is very risky politics," Tsang said.

Hanson, a former fish and chip shop proprietor from conservative Queensland, has attracted support from about 10 percent of the country's voters with her criticism of immigration, multi-culturalism, Aboriginal welfare and tariff reduction.
